pitch: A business novel that teaches the theory of constraints: a system's throughput depends on its bottleneck.
quiz: What is the goal of a manufacturing company according to Jonah?
Maximize machine utilization
Make money, now and in the future
Produce the best possible quality
Increase market share
Everything else—quality, technology, productivity—is only a means to this goal.
How does Jonah define throughput?
The number of parts produced
The rate at which the system generates money through sales
The speed of the fastest machine
Forecast revenue
A part produced but not sold is not throughput, only inventory.
What does Alex learn from Herbie on the hike?
That you must speed up the fastest
That the group moves at the speed of the slowest
That you should leave earlier
That everyone's packs should be lighter
The system's pace is set by its constraint; helping Herbie speeds up the whole group.
What does the matches-and-dice game illustrate?
Chance always evens out
In a dependent chain, delays spread and gains are lost
Each step must be perfectly balanced
Averages are reliable
Dependent events and statistical fluctuations doom a “balanced” plant to inventory and delays.
What does an hour lost at a bottleneck cost?
The machine's hourly cost
Nothing, it will be made up later
An hour of output for the entire plant
The operator's wage
The bottleneck sets total throughput: every hour lost there is lost for the whole system.
What should a non-bottleneck resource do?
Produce at maximum
Work at the bottleneck's pace, even if it sometimes sits idle
Be eliminated
Build safety stock
Activating a resource beyond what the bottleneck absorbs only produces inventory.
What does the “rope” represent in drum-buffer-rope?
The link between the bottleneck and the release of materials
The assembly line
The contract with the customer
The bottleneck's queue
New materials are released only at the pace the bottleneck consumes them.
What is the right sequence of the five steps?
Elevate, identify, exploit, subordinate, repeat
Identify, exploit, subordinate, elevate, repeat
Exploit, identify, elevate, subordinate, repeat
Subordinate, identify, elevate, exploit, repeat
Exploit existing capacity before investing to increase it.
